summary: H.R. 7037, the DOMINANCE Act, aims to promote energy and critical mineral security for the United States and its allies. The bill establishes a Bureau of Energy Security and Diplomacy within the Department of State, creates multi-year Energy Security Compacts with partner countries, authorizes U.S. participation in the Minerals Security Partnership, and sets up fellowship and visiting scholar programs focused on the mining industry.

affected_groups.effect: Eligible to receive fellowships to study and conduct research at foreign mining institutions.
affected_groups.group: U.S. university students and graduates in STEM and mining fields

affected_groups.effect: Eligible to participate in placement programs at U.S. institutions of higher education to advance research and education.
May enter into Energy Security Compacts with the U.S. to receive technical support, grants, and capacity-building assistance for energy and mineral sectors.

key_provisions: Establishes a Bureau of Energy Security and Diplomacy and an Assistant Secretary position at the State Department to handle international energy and critical mineral policies.
Authorizes multi-year Energy Security Compacts between the U.S. and eligible partner countries to increase reliable access to energy and critical minerals.
Authorizes U.S. participation in the Minerals Security Partnership to support investment in critical mineral mining, processing, and refining projects.
Creates the Critical Mineral Mining Fellowship Program within the Fulbright exchange program to send U.S. students to foreign mining institutions.
Creates the Visiting Mining Scholars Program to bring foreign mining academics and professionals to U.S. institutions of higher education.
Authorizes U.S. membership in the International Nickel Study Group.
Establishes an interagency Energy Security Compacts Council to coordinate compact-related activities across federal departments.
missing_information: Exact dollar amounts authorized to be appropriated for the various programs, grants, and fellowships.
The specific criteria or identity of all countries that will qualify as 'partner countries' or members of the Minerals Security Partnership beyond general eligibility thresholds.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 7037, the DOMINANCE Act, aims to promote energy and critical mineral security for the United States and its allies. The bill establishes a Bureau of Energy Security and Diplomacy within the Department of State, creates multi-year Energy Security Compacts with partner countries, authorizes U.S. participation in the Minerals Security Partnership, and sets up fellowship and visiting scholar programs focused on the mining industry.
summary_detail.significance: This bill significantly reshapes U.S. diplomatic and economic engagement regarding global energy and critical mineral supply chains, aiming to reduce dependence on adversarial nations like China. It sets up new bureaucratic offices, interagency councils, international compacts, and educational programs backed by federal funding transfers and hiring flexibilities.

title: Developing Overseas Mineral Investments and New Allied Networks for Critical Energies Act
